grammar.title: 3B: Articles - a / an, the, no article
grammar.explanation:
Use **a** when you say what something is for the first time. I see **a car**.

Use **an** before a vowel sound: a, e, i, o, u. It is **an airport**.

Use **the** when you talk about the same thing again. I see **a bus**. **The bus** is big.

Use **the** when it is clear which one you mean. **The station** is near my house.

Use **the** for the only one, like **the moon**. We say **the train** when we both know the train. I have **the ticket**.

Use no article to talk about things in general. **Bikes** are cheap. **Roads** are long.

Use no article with **home**, **work**, and **school** after at, to, or from. I go to **work** by **taxi**.

Use no article with meals and days. I eat **breakfast** before my **plane**.
examples: It is *a car*. (saying what something is)
She went to *an airport*. (an before a vowel sound)
We waited at *the station*. (clear which one)
*The moon* is in the sky. (the only one)
*The train* is very fast. (we know the train)
I bought *a ticket* for the train. (first mention)
I go to *work* by *bike*. (no article with work)
He is at *home* now. (no article with home)
We have *breakfast* at seven. (no article with meals)
We took *a taxi* to the airport. (first mention)
*The plane* left at eight. (we know the plane)
